source: DP AFCAT Practice Bank v0 (Claude Doc 'AFCAT Practice Bank - 300 Original Questions', rev 3, 2026-11-03)
notes: v2 (2026-11-04): replaced the 10 easiest items with harder ones, added a 4-blank cloze passage, replaced dated current affairs with four verified 2026 items, and added six original figure-based reasoning items.
All items are DP-original practice questions written to the AFCAT pattern. None is an official or memory-reconstructed AFCAT paper question.
Section order follows the AFCAT paper: GA, English, Numerical, Reasoning. 25/30/20/25 is DP's split, not an official IAF allocation.
Figures live in assets/fm01 as SVG with alt text and hashes; the learner API does not serve question images yet.
Current-affairs items carry source_evidence and a recheck_on date.
Difficulty labels are author estimates, not calibrated.

stem.text: The main idea of the passage is that:
stem.passage: Air power has transformed modern warfare. Unlike armies, which must cross terrain, an air force can strike at depth within hours and shift its effort from one theatre to another with little delay. Yet air power alone rarely wins a war. Its true strength lies in partnership with land and naval forces, where it provides surveillance, transport and precision fire. Moreover, technology has made pilots dependent on a vast network of engineers, technicians and controllers on the ground. A single sortie is therefore the visible tip of an enormous, disciplined effort.

options.text: Air power is powerful but depends on joint effort and a large support network

explanation.text: The passage praises air power's reach but stresses partnership with other forces and a ground support network.

stem.text: In the passage, choose the word that best fills blank (1).
stem.passage: Every pilot learns early that the sky is (1) ______ to carelessness. A small error that would pass (2) ______ on the ground can, at altitude, turn into an emergency within seconds. That is why flight training places such (3) ______ on checklists, which leave nothing to memory alone. Over time these routines become second nature, so that when the unexpected happens, the pilot can respond (4) ______ rather than react in panic.

explanation.text: 'Hostile to carelessness' fits the warning tone: the sky punishes careless flying. The other words reverse or blur the meaning.

stem.text: Choose the correct mirror image of the given figure when the mirror is placed along the line M.

assets.alt: A flag on a pole, with the triangular flag at the top pointing right, a short bar to the right of the pole and a small circle at lower right. A vertical mirror line M is on the right.

Four answer figures. A: flag at the top pointing right, pole on the left, circle at lower right. B: flag at the bottom pointing right, pole on the left, circle at upper right. C: flag at the bottom pointing left, pole on the right, circle at upper left. D: flag at the top pointing left, pole on the right, circle at lower left.

explanation.text: A vertical mirror swaps left and right but keeps top and bottom. The flag must point left with the pole on the right, and the circle stays at the bottom. (A) is the original, (B) is the water image and (C) is a half-turn.

stem.text: Choose the correct water image of the given figure (the water line is below the figure).

assets.alt: A staircase line rising from bottom-left to top-right ending in an arrowhead pointing right, a small circle at upper left and a filled square at lower right. A horizontal water line is below the figure.

Four answer figures. A: staircase descends from top-left to an arrowhead at lower right; circle at lower left; square at upper right. B: staircase rises from bottom-right to an arrowhead at upper left; circle at upper right; square at lower left. C: staircase descends from top-right to an arrowhead at lower left; circle at lower right; square at upper left. D: the figure turned a quarter-turn clockwise, staircase running top to bottom with the arrowhead pointing down at lower right.

explanation.text: A water image flips top and bottom but keeps left and right. The arrowhead stays on the right but the staircase now descends towards it. (B) is the mirror image, (C) a half-turn and (D) a quarter-turn.

stem.text: A square sheet is folded and punched as shown in figures (1) to (3). How will it look when unfolded?

assets.alt: Step 1: a square sheet is folded along its vertical centre line, left half onto right. Step 2: the folded sheet is folded along its horizontal centre line, top half onto bottom. Step 3: one hole is punched in the folded quarter, near its lower-left area.

Four unfolded squares. A: two holes in the lower half, side by side. B: four holes in the middle band near the left and right edges. C: two holes on a diagonal. D: four holes, one in each quarter, placed symmetrically about both centre lines.

explanation.text: Unfold the second fold first: the hole is reflected about the horizontal centre line, giving two holes. Unfolding the first fold reflects both about the vertical centre line, giving four holes placed symmetrically, one in each quarter.
